title: Vayakhel: he gathered them (Exodus 35:1)
hookLine: after the golden calf, Moses gathers everyone together again

cards: A word in this week's portion turned up a few chapters back, at a dark moment. When Moses was late coming down the mountain, the people crowded around Aaron and demanded a god to go before them.

The JPS translation says "the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron". That gathering made a golden calf. Now Moses is down, with new tablets, and the first thing he does in this portion uses the same Hebrew verb.
Same people. Same root. A completely different kind of gathering.

teach.b: The portion is named for its first word, vayakhel, and he assembled. In the JPS 1917 translation: "And Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel."
The root is three Hebrew letters, kuf, hey, lamed, and it means to gather people into one body. From that same root comes today's word, kehillah, a community.
Tradition calls a Jewish town's organized community its kehillah, and sometimes a kehillah kedoshah, a holy community.
The book of Ecclesiastes is called Kohelet in Hebrew, a name traditionally read as the gatherer, from the same root.
Now set the two gatherings side by side. The first time, the people gather themselves against their leader, out of fear and impatience, and make an idol.

This time, Moses gathers all of them, and the first thing he tells them about is Shabbat: six days of work, a seventh of rest. Then he asks for gifts for the sanctuary, from everyone whose heart is willing.
Some commentators hear a repair in this: the same energy that built a calf can build a sanctuary. A crowd isn't good or bad by itself.
What matters is what it gathers around.
Jewish prayer keeps that idea close: certain prayers are said only with a minyan, ten gathered together.

how: Jewish communal life is organized around the kehillah, and certain prayers, such as the Kaddish, Barchu and the public Torah reading, are traditionally said only with a minyan of ten.

o: a synagogue building where people come to pray
the quorum of ten needed for public prayer
a community: people gathered into one body

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.

s: the verb for Moses gathering the people appears earlier, at the golden calf
the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron: same root, very different gathering.
the first thing Moses tells the gathered people about is the sanctuary's gold
he begins with Shabbat, then asks for gifts.
kehillah and Kohelet share a root
kuf, hey, lamed: to gather people together.

games.q: you're Moses, back from the mountain after the golden calf. the people are ashamed and scattered. what do you do first?
games.why: vayakhel: Moses assembles all the congregation. the verb that built a calf now gathers a people to build a sanctuary.

practice: Think of people around you who don't see each other enough: neighbors, cousins, old friends. Picture what could bring a few of them together for something good, a meal, a walk, a visit to someone lonely, and who would come.
Keep it small and real, and sit with the picture of them in one room.

wordCard.voice: Kehillah. A community, people gathered into one body. From the same root as vayakhel, and Moses assembled them.

orig.note: Hebrew: a community, from the root kuf-hey-lamed, to gather.

carryVoice: Your line: gather the people. A community is people in a room for something. Day three hundred sixty-eight, done.
